item.title: Arts funding reconsideration heads to March 3 County Council agenda
item.description: The Volusia County Council will consider releasing funding for the 2025–26 Community Cultural Grant Program during its March 3 meeting in DeLand, after a majority vote to bring the issue back for discussion amid significant public response. item.title: Popular DeLand secondhand store set to reopen March 3
item.description: More than two months after it was closed for remodeling, the Elite Repeat popular secondhand store in DeLand is preparing to welcome back its bargain-seeking customers. The thrift store, located at 720 S. Woodland Blvd. and operated by the AdventHealth DeLand hospital, will reopen with a ribbon-cutting set for 11 a.m. Tuesday, March 3. The store offers cut-rate prices on […] The post Popular DeLand secondhand store set to reopen March 3 first appeared on The West Volusia Beacon.

item.title: 16 oaks removed at admin center in Downtown DeLand
item.description: Volusia County’s Thomas C. Kelly Administration Center in Downtown DeLand is looking pretty naked these days, after 16 oaks that graced the north and west sides of the massive building were removed. item.title: DeLand salutes super students
item.description: Following a monthly tradition of the DeLand City Commission, Super Star Students for the month of March were recognized at the opening of the March 2 City Commission meeting. item.title: Glenwood Cemetery reflects the community’s compassion
item.description: Editor, The Beacon: This letter acknowledges the tireless work and devotion Glenwood residents have for their historic cemetery at Guava Street and Rogers Road, in unincorporated DeLand. item.title: What future do we want for Deltona?
item.description: Editor, The Beacon: When we ask what Deltona will look like in 25 years, we are not asking an abstract planning question.
